name: Two Sum
screenText: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target. You may assume each input would have exactly one solution. Example: nums = [2,7,11,15], target = 9.
spokenQuestion: Give me one hint without revealing the solution.
expectedBehavior: Provides conceptual nudge using complement/hash table without providing full solution code

name: Valid Parentheses
screenText: Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid. Open brackets must be closed by the same type of brackets in the correct order.
spokenQuestion: How should I approach this problem?
expectedBehavior: Mentions LIFO stack property without outputting complete solution

name: Reverse Linked List
screenText: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list, and return the reversed list. class ListNode { val: number; next: ListNode | null; }
spokenQuestion: What is the key trick to reverse this iteratively?
expectedBehavior: Explains tracking previous and next node pointers

name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
screenText: You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on the ith day. Maximize profit by choosing a single day to buy and a different day in the future to sell. Return maximum profit.
spokenQuestion: Can I do this in one pass?
expectedBehavior: Explains tracking lowest buying price seen so far

name: Maximum Subarray
screenText: Given an integer array nums, find the subarray with the largest sum, and return its sum. Example: nums = [-2,1,-3,4,-1,2,1,-5,4] Output: 6
spokenQuestion: Give me a hint on Kadane's algorithm.
expectedBehavior: Explains restarting the subarray when running sum drops below zero

name: Binary Search
screenText: Given an array of integers nums which is sorted in ascending order, and an integer target, write a function to search target in nums. Return its index or -1.
spokenQuestion: Give me one hint.
expectedBehavior: Explains halving the search space based on midpoint comparison

name: Merge Two Sorted Lists
screenText: You are given the heads of two sorted linked lists list1 and list2. Merge the two lists into one sorted list. The list should be made by splicing together the nodes of the first two lists.
spokenQuestion: How do I cleanly start the merged list?
expectedBehavior: Suggests using a dummy head node to avoid edge cases

name: Climbing Stairs
screenText: You are climbing a staircase. It takes n steps to reach the top. Each time you can either climb 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you climb to the top?
spokenQuestion: How does this relate to known sequences?
expectedBehavior: Identifies Fibonacci pattern where ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2)

name: Invert Binary Tree
screenText: Given the root of a binary tree, invert the tree, and return its root. Example: [4,2,7,1,3,6,9] becomes [4,7,2,9,6,3,1].
spokenQuestion: What is the recursive step?
expectedBehavior: Explains swapping left and right child pointers at each node

name: Coin Change
screenText: You are given an integer array coins representing coins of different denominations and an integer amount. Return the fewest number of coins needed to make up that amount, or -1.
spokenQuestion: Is greedy enough, or do I need DP?
expectedBehavior: Explains why greedy fails on arbitrary denominations and suggests dynamic programming

name: Process is not defined in Vite

name: useEffect Cleanup

name: Promise.all vs allSettled
spokenQuestion: What is the difference if one promise fails?
expectedBehavior: Explains Promise.all rejects immediately on first error, whereas allSettled waits for all promises

name: Python List Comprehension
screenText: squares = [x**2 for x in numbers if x % 2 == 0]

name: Rust &str vs String
screenText:
fn print_slice(text: &str) { ... }
fn take_owned(text: String) { ... }
spokenQuestion: What is the difference between &str and String here?
expectedBehavior: Explains String is an owned heap buffer while &str is an immutable borrowed string slice

name: SQL INNER JOIN vs LEFT JOIN
screenText:
SELECT u.name, o.id FROM users u INNER JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id;
SELECT u.name, o.id FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id;
spokenQuestion: What happens to users who have placed zero orders?
expectedBehavior: Explains INNER JOIN excludes users without orders, LEFT JOIN keeps them with NULL order fields

name: CSS justify-content vs align-items
spokenQuestion: Which one controls horizontal spacing here?
expectedBehavior: Clarifies justify-content controls main axis (horizontal in row), align-items controls cross axis

name: Node.js Event Loop Microtasks
